seoDescription: Learn step-by-step how to create and customize app icons and splash screens for Ionic 6+ apps using Capacitor for Android and iOS. This tutorial covers preparing 1024×1024 icons and large splash assets, installing Capacitor resources tooling and Splash Screen plugin, adding platforms, resolving Android adaptive icon errors, configuring capacitor.config, and generating correctly scaled iOS launch images to avoid stretching.

chapters.title: Introduction and project setup
chapters.description: Overview of the video's goals and initial Ionic project creation in Visual Studio Code.

chapters.title: Preparing resources folder and installation notes
chapters.description: Create a resources folder with PNGs, review Capacitor docs, and install the resources tool required to generate images.

chapters.title: Adding platforms and generating resources
chapters.description: Run Ionic build, add iOS and Android via Capacitor, then generate icon and splash resources for each platform.

chapters.title: Fixing Android adaptive icon errors in Android Studio
chapters.description: Use Android Studio's Image Asset tool to create foreground/background adaptive icons and resolve resource linking errors.

chapters.title: Installing Splash Screen plugin and configuring Capacitor
chapters.description: Install the Capacitor Splash Screen plugin, update capacitor.config.ts settings like launchShowDuration and autoHide, and sync platforms.

chapters.title: Testing on emulators and device; iOS scaling issues
chapters.description: Run on emulators and physical Android device, note emulator limitations, and investigate iOS splash scaling differences.

chapters.title: Generating iOS launch images and final testing
chapters.description: Use Image Gorilla (or similar) to generate iOS-specific launch images at multiple scales, import them into Xcode, and verify splash screens and icons on devices.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Capacitor resources tooling**: install the Capacitor/Ionic resource generator globally and run the platform-specific commands to generate icons and splash screens for Android and iOS.

- **Image source sizes**: use **1024×1024** for icons and use large square images for splash generation; the presenter used **2732×2732** initially and switched to **4096×4096** for better iOS results.

- **Platform steps**:
  - Run **ionic build** to produce the www folder.
  - Add platforms with **ionic cap add ios/android**.
  - Generate resources using the provided Capacitor resource commands for each platform.

- **Android adaptive icons**: fix resource linking errors by creating adaptive foreground/background assets in Android Studio (Right-click res → New → Image Asset), trim or resize foreground, and set a background color hex if needed.

- **Splash Screen plugin & config**:
  - Install the Capacitor **Splash Screen** plugin and required helper packages.
  - Configure **capacitor.config.ts**: set **launchShowDuration** (e.g., 3000 ms), **launchAutoHide**, **backgroundColor**, **splashName**, **androidScaleType**, **showSpinner** etc.

- **Emulator vs device**: emulator behavior can differ; test on a real Android device when emulators don’t show splash screens correctly.

- **iOS launch images**: to avoid stretching on iOS, generate explicit launch images for iPhone/iPad at multiple scales (1x, 2x, 3x) — the presenter used Image Gorilla to produce a bundle of correctly sized launch images, then drag-and-dropped them into Xcode asset slots.

## Practical Tips

> [!TIP] Use a large square source (4096×4096) for splash generation when you need many iOS sizes to avoid scaling artifacts.

> [!NOTE] Android supports scale-type options (fitXY, centerCrop) in Capacitor config; many of these options are Android-specific.

> [!IMPORTANT] If Android Studio reports "resource linking failed" for adaptive icons, recreate the image assets (foreground/background) and ensure names match and files are overwritten.

## Takeaways

- Follow the resource generation workflow: prepare high-resolution sources → build → add platforms → generate resources → fix platform-specific issues in Android Studio or Xcode → install Splash Screen plugin → configure capacitor.config.ts → sync and test on real devices.

- Generating platform-specific asset bundles (rather than relying on a single universal image) prevents stretching and ensures crisp icons and splash screens across devices.
